The measured history on this page is explicit that a household subsidy did not pay (PM Surya Ghar: 1.8x basket median against a 2.0x market median, 0% made 5x). Not mapped, no name added.

govt_considered.release: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh to chair National Review Meeting on SVAMITVA Scheme in New Delhi tomorrow
govt_considered.verdict: NOT A DECISION — an advance notice of a review meeting. The ₹1,769 crore is SVAMITVA's existing sanctioned outlay, not a new allocation, and nothing was approved, sanctioned or awarded. SVAMITVA is drone-based village land survey work, so a genuine new tranche would be mappable to drone-survey and geospatial contractors — but a meeting notice is not that tranche, and the standing rule is never to add a name on a hunch. Not mapped, no name added.

researched.name: KP Green Engineering Ltd
researched.reason: Order book ₹460 cr (30-Sep-2025) → ₹1,892 cr (30-Sep-2026), +311% on comparable definitions, both ends read from the company's own call transcripts; 1.36x trailing sales. The interesting part is the other side: H1 FY27 revenue +27% but PAT −41% on finance costs up 117% and depreciation up 356% from the Matar capacity, and the stock is −54% in a year. The promoter is subscribing ₹100 cr of warrants at ₹292, 23.9% ABOVE the ₹235.75 close. Against it: the jump is six months old and the book has been flat for two quarters; FY27 guidance of ₹1,700–1,800 cr needs 49–64% more revenue in H2 than H1; related-party sales were 49.6% of FY26 revenue (₹617.22 cr, computed from the annual report's RPT note) with ₹238 cr of purchases from the same group and ₹19.19 cr of royalty paid to the promoter personally; and with eight order filings in two years the rarity study puts it in the bucket that reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x never. Published at medium confidence with all of that stated.

researched.name: Susan Electricals India Ltd
researched.reason: ₹148.90 cr of new orders in the seven weeks to 18-Nov-2026 (incl GST), of which ₹85 cr is HT cables and MVCC; order book ₹203 cr as on 18-Nov against ₹147 cr at 30-Sep. That is 37.0% of a trailing year's sales (31.4% ex-GST), inside the 25–50% bucket the order study rates best. H1 FY27 revenue ₹202.06 cr (+190%) and PAT ₹13.15 cr (+191%); HT/MVCC went from ₹0.52 cr to ₹39 cr of sales in a year; capacity 11,000 → 16,000 km of cable and 3,307 → 4,200 → 5,500 t of winding wire. Stock closed at its 52-week low ₹181.40 the same day, −42% in three months. Published at LOW confidence: five months listed, no annual report, no related-party note, no disclosed debt, no disclosed utilisation, no product-wise margin (the only published segment figures were mislabelled and withdrawn on the call), a BSE discrepancy on the limited review report, a secretarial auditor resigned with immediate effect in September, and the whole case rests on a CCV line that no document confirms is actually running.

researched.name: Tipco Engineering India Ltd
researched.reason: The results clear the trigger bar easily — H1 FY27 total income ₹74.02 cr (+47.3%), EBITDA ₹23.49 cr (+72.0%, margin 31.74%), PAT ₹16.50 cr (+92%), EPS ₹7.95 — and the DRDO/HEMRL vendor approval, the 51% defence/robotics subsidiary TDTRPL, the LexaMix German-technology tie-up and ₹60 cr of planned capex (3.26 acres at Satara for ₹7.15 cr, a new Pune facility, a 4–5 acre Sonipat expansion) are all real. **Held back because the dominant new fact is a related-party acquisition disclosed without its numbers.** The company will consolidate ALL promoter-group businesses, including Ranks and Hanutech, into the listed entity; both press releases read in full give only ‘approximately 6x current earnings’ and ‘EPS accretive from Day 1’ — **no consideration, no share-swap ratio, no share count, no revenue or PAT for either target, no valuer named** — while stating that the promoter and the targets' partners will acquire equity in TIPCO. So the dilution and the price paid to related parties cannot be measured from any document, and the stock closed at its 52-week high of ₹376.55 after +83.9% in three months and +141.8% in six. Revisit when the scheme, the valuation report or the swap ratio is filed.

researched.name: Apex Frozen Foods Ltd
researched.reason: Top-scoring candidate (9.0) and a genuine trade-remedy event, but it runs AGAINST the company. From the Q2/H1 FY27 transcript (call 16-Nov-2026, filed 19-Nov): the US Department of Commerce's final determinations revised its anti-dumping duty rate from **1.35% to 3.76% and then to 5.53%**, and the audit committee decided to provide **₹10.10 cr in Q2 FY27 against an incremental ADD liability of roughly ₹30 cr** relating to earlier years, which the company describes as a contingent liability; an appeal is filed before the US Court of International Trade. The US reciprocal tariff of 10% also still applies, and the US was 62% of Q2 volumes and 66% of H1. This page's trade lane exists to catch beneficiaries of protection, not its targets, and the standing rule is no short ideas. Liquidity also fails the triage test: median daily turnover ₹24.7 lakh, below the ₹25 lakh floor. The operating half was good (H1 revenue ₹530 cr +7%, EBITDA ₹51 cr +40% at a 9.4% margin, PBT before exceptionals ₹42 cr +60%, PAT ₹24 cr +13%; Q2 volumes 2,973 MT +14% at ₹874/kg). Carried as the trade/commodity watch line: the thing that would turn it is the India–EU FTA taking the EU tariff from 4.3%/7.2% to 0%, which management says it has been ‘informed’ is tentatively early 2027 with the outcome unknown, plus the CIT appeal. **Note: the duty rates here are read from the company's own transcript; the US DOC determination itself was not opened in this run.**
